ends.note: east part of Pennock Alley dead-ends at a building (pasted correction) about 70 px short of Mound Street
Cedar Alley dead-ends at a building line well short of Mound Street

notes: Pennock Alley jogs at Cutter: the west part (lines y 1442/1490 at Cutter, 16 ft) and the east part (lines y 1358/1412) do not overlap, so they are recorded as two T-junctions on Cutter. The 9th-8th street printed BERNARD (no suffix, about 12 ft, 12' printed at 8th) runs from 9th to 8th and ends at 8th. The unnamed passage printed only ALLEY runs north from 9th, on the line of Bernard, to Cedar Alley (about 12 ft, centre x ~2771), so 9th/Bernard is recorded as a crossing and the ALLEY/Cedar junction as a T with '' as the name. Kossuth Street is not printed on this sheet: the narrow street (about 19 ft, block lines x 830/898) entering West Court from the north is named from the key map. The '?' at x 3102 is another narrow street (about 12 ft, block lines x 3081/3122) entering West Court from the north with its own water main, unlabelled on this sheet and the key map. Notre Dame Place (printed NOTRE DAME PL., with (CONVENT PL.) under it, 25 ft) runs south from West Court only as far as Pennock Alley; it is offset about 80 px east of the '?' street. Rittenhouse Street enters West Court from the north at the extreme west edge: only its east block line (x 362) is drawn, so its centre (x ~274) is estimated from a 50 ft width and sits on the edge of the drawn area. Cedar Alley is printed 16' at the west edge and 12' east of Cutter. Mound Street is printed 47'. The sheet is slightly rotated: West Court's centre drifts from y ~950 at the west edge to ~919 at Mound, and Mound and Cutter lean east going south.
